rawSourceText: Commitment authority represents an upper limit up to which task teams can commit future disbursements at the individual TF level. The asset classes that can be committed against are either (i) cash, (ii) cash plus promissory notes, or (iii) cash plus promissory notes and contributions receivable. The default BoC for a trust fund is cash, but may be modified to include promissory notes receivable and/or contributions receivable with the approval of Director(s) in the unit managing the trust fund. nextSourceText: Cash received from DPs contributions, loans from DPs and proceeds from the issuance of bonds (for IFFIM) are managed by IBRD’s Treasury, which manages a commingled investment portfolio (the Pool) for all funds that are administered by the B

rawSourceText: Cash received from DPs contributions, loans from DPs and proceeds from the issuance of bonds (for IFFIM) are managed by IBRD’s Treasury, which manages a commingled investment portfolio (the Pool) for all funds that are administered by the Bank Group entities. The Pool also includes funds held in ICSID's escrow accounts. IBRD maintains all assets underlying the trust funds’ fund balances separate and apart from the assets of the World Bank Group. IBRD, on behalf of the World Bank Group, invests the funds in liquid financial instruments such as government and agency obligations, time deposits, money-market securities and asset-backed securities, as well as swaps and a range of other derivative instruments. Additionally, the pool also include equity securities. The investment composition within the pool is based on the investment horizons and cash flow profiles of the trust fund programs. Net investment income earned by the Pool is allocated to each trust fund based on its share of cash and investments in the Pool.
